subject: FinEx throughput sizing: post-call follow-up and clarifications
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@finex-payments.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@finex-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-25T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: FinEx throughput sizing: post-call follow-up and clarifications

Hi Alice / Tom,

Thanks for the time today — good discussion on expected traffic patterns and UX constraints. Per our call, I wanted to capture the follow-up items and a couple of clarifying questions so we can size a recommended config and put together a quote.

Recap / what we heard from FinEx:
- Primary use case: customer support assistant inside banking UI (interactive).
- Streaming required for progressive responses.
- Latency target discussed: interactive target ~250ms p95 for token delivery, with 500ms p95 as a softer acceptable bound.
- Peak vs steady: you mentioned large bursts during payroll/statement runs, and steadier traffic otherwise.

Clarifying questions (to size throughput):
1) Average tokens per request (prompt + completion) — we discussed ~100–150 but please confirm an average or distribution.
2) Peak QPS and burst duration (e.g., 30 QPS sustained for 5–10 minutes, or 30 QPS spikes for <1 minute?).
3) Concurrent streams (how many simultaneous open streaming responses at peak?).
4) Percent of requests that need streaming vs. batched non-streaming responses.

Next steps from Redwood:
- If you can share a quick workload profile (tokens per request, QPS histogram, concurrency and burst durations) we'll produce an initial throughput sizing worksheet and recommended Dedicated config.
- We'll also call out options for achieving the latency SLO (autoscaling strategy, batching/caching knobs, and streaming considerations).

I've attached a blank template (finex_workload_profile.xlsx) you can fill if that's easiest.

Thanks — Rafael

Subject: Re: FinEx throughput sizing: post-call follow-up and clarifications

Rafael — thanks for the recap and the template. Attaching the filled workload profile (finex_workload_profile.xlsx). Answers inline below.

Summary of our workload (from profile):
- Average tokens per request (prompt + completion): 120 tokens (prompt ~80, completion ~40).
- Typical steady-state QPS: 4 QPS.
- Peak QPS during business events: up to 30 QPS sustained for ~10 minutes; short spikes up to ~60 QPS for <60 seconds.
- Typical concurrent open streams at peak: ~25 active browser streams (users waiting for progressive response).
- Percentage using streaming: ~90% (interactive UI), 10% are background batch jobs where streaming not required.
- Latency requirement: p95 token delivery target 250ms; p95 full response 500ms acceptable. For background jobs, 1–2s is fine.
- Region: primary US users, small EU presence (~5%).

Let us know if you need more granularity on QPS distribution.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Zhang
Sr. Product Manager, FinEx Payments
alice.zhang@finex-payments.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@finex-payments.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@finex-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-27T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinEx throughput sizing: post-call follow-up and clarifications

Alice — perfect, that helps a lot. Quick notes based on the numbers you shared and proposed next steps.

Sizing math (very high level):
- Peak tokens/sec = peak QPS * tokens_per_request = 30 QPS * 120 tokens = 3,600 tokens/sec sustained for the ~10-minute peak window.
- Short spikes: 60 QPS -> 7,200 tokens/sec for <60s.
- Steady tokens/sec = 4 QPS * 120 = 480 tokens/sec.
- Concurrency ~= number of in-flight streaming responses (you reported ~25 at peak). Our runtime treats streaming similarly to in-flight requests for KV cache and memory but has lower batching opportunity since latency matters.

Initial sizing considerations:
- For interactive p95 token delivery ~250ms we prioritize low-latency execution and smaller batching windows. That increases per-token cost vs. aggressive batching.
- To handle 3,600 tokens/sec sustained with headroom for spikes, a conservative Dedicated pool estimate is: 1-2 high-memory A100-style GPUs (or equivalent H100/80GB configs) with autoscale for short spikes. We'll produce a more precise recommendation after we run the provided profile through our sizing tool.

Questions before we finalize the worksheet:
1) For the 10-minute sustained peak, do you expect this to happen several times per day or only during known business events (e.g., payroll runs)?
2) For the short spikes to 60 QPS, what percentage of total daily traffic do those represent? (helps with autoscaling economics).
3) Can you confirm the acceptable SLA for availability? We typically size differently for 99.9% vs 99.95% targets.

Proposed next steps:
- I'll run the attached profile through our throughput tool and share a short PDF recap with two sizing options (cost-optimized and low-latency/high-headroom).
- Marissa (cc) will do a quick check on the SLA and any procurement constraints.
- Can we schedule a 30-minute sizing workshop next week to walk through the numbers and tradeoffs? Available windows: Tue/Wed morning PT.

Thanks — Rafael

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@finex-payments.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@finex-payments.com>

Date: 2026-08-30T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinEx throughput sizing: post-call follow-up and clarifications

Hi Alice / Tom,

Thanks for the profile — I ran it through our sizing tool and attached a short recap (redwood_throughput_recap.pdf) with two recommended configurations:

Option A — Low-latency (recommended for interactive UX):
- Dedicated pool: 2 x A100 80GB equivalent (or 2 x H100, if available)
- Autoscale policy: +1 node on sustained >2 minutes above 75% utilization; burst capacity to handle 60 QPS spikes automatically
- Expected p95 token delivery: ~200–300ms depending on prompt length; cost: higher than option B

Option B — Cost-optimized (good if you can accept slightly higher latency during peaks):
- Dedicated pool: 1 x A100 80GB equivalent + burst credits for 60 QPS spikes
- Aggressive micro-batching during steady-state to reduce per-token cost
- Expected p95 token delivery: ~300–500ms during peaks; cost: ~30% lower

Other notes:
- Streaming: both options support SSE/websocket streaming. We recommend keeping ~90% of requests streaming (as you noted) and allowing background batch work to be non-streaming.
- SLA: Rafael, please confirm if FinEx needs 99.95% availability. If so, we should size for an active-standby across AZs which increases cost ~15%.

Next steps for FinEx:
1) Confirm frequency of the 10-minute sustained peaks (several times/day vs. infrequent events).
2) Confirm availability SLA (99.9% vs. 99.95%).
3) Book a 30-minute sizing workshop — Rafael and I are available Tue/Wed 9–11am PT next week.

I'll leave scheduling with Rafael. Thanks — Marissa

Marissa Cole
